details.publicNotes:
Often mistaken for harmless cannonball mangroves, these predatory trees lurk in warm, brackish coastal waters. They mainly prey on animals but have been known to attack travelers or small boats that get too close. Their hunting strategy is as simple as it is gruesome: they bombard their prey with cannonball-like fruits, the most developed of which immediately deploy into infantile gungroves and begin feeding on their designated fertilizer even before it succumbs to their burgeoning roots. Those who are downed by the impact itself are absorbed just as greedily by the adult tree.

Though the sound of cannonfruit firing is reminiscent of the boom of a cannon, the plant's internal mechanisms have nothing to do with flames. Instead, a gungrove's trunk contains specialized channels that allow it to rapidly manipulate water pressure, creating hollow voids that water rushes into at breakneck speeds. Efforts to create a tame cultivar of gungroves have failed dramatically so far, though rumors abound of unscrupulous pirates and corrupt port officials feeding their enemies to "pet" gungroves.

Fruits of Healing

Paradoxically, the fruit of a gungrove tree is highly valued for its medicinal properties. When boiled, the peel of a cannonfruit produces a tea known to soothe digestive pains, while the seeds can be cooked and ground into a poultice as a remedy for rashes. Some have even claimed that cannonfruit, when properly prepared, can cure magical maladies. Unfortunately, collecting the fruit often results in wounds that no herbal remedy can heal.

description.value: The gungrove can spend 1 minute to plant itself in an area of shallow water. Until the next time the gungrove acts, it has an automatic result of 32 on Deception checks and DCs to pass as an inanimate mangrove tree.
Though it's quickest in water, the gungrove's roots are also dexterous on land. It can Step 10 feet and doesn't treat shallow water as difficult terrain.

Trigger The gungrove critically hits with a cannonfruit Strike

Effect The gungrove uses Deploy Sapling.

Requirements The gungrove's last action was a successful cannonfruit Strike against a Small or larger living creature

Effect The fruit deploys into a sapling, trying to get its roots into the creature it struck. The creature attempts a @Check[reflex|dc:20] save.

Critical Success The creature is unaffected.

Success The sapling fails to take hold, but its roots still hamper the creature's movement. The creature takes –5-foot circumstance penalty to its Speeds for 1 round or until it Escapes, whichever comes first.

Failure Until the creature Escapes the sapling, it is @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.4D2KBtexWXa6oUMR]{Drained 1} and takes a –5-foot circumstance penalty to its Speeds.

Critical Failure Until the creature Escapes the sapling, it is @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.4D2KBtexWXa6oUMR]{Drained 2} and takes a –15-foot circumstance penalty to its Speeds. After escaping the fruit, the creature is drained 1 for 1 minute.

The gungrove propels itself out of water in a burst of immature cannonfruit. It Swims up to its Speed in a straight line, then Leaps up to 20 feet. At the end of its movement, creatures within a @Template[type:emanation|distance:10] around the gungrove take @Damage[2d6[bludgeoning]|options:area-damage] damage (@Check[reflex|dc:20|basic] save); those that fail the saving throw are pushed 5 feet away from the gungrove.
